I installed gbrain v0.60.734.0. `gbrain --version` prints `gbrain 0.60.734.0` in a new login shell.

- **What I ran:** the docs give `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` in `README.md`, `INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS.md`. I ran that command with your tag in place of `#stable`: `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#v0.60.734.0`. It installed commit `a278ddf`. Right now the `stable` tag points to that same commit.
- **Bun:** gbrain needs Bun 1.4.4 or newer, and this machine had none. I used the official installer, which put Bun 1.4.4 in `~/.bun/bin`.
- **PATH:** I added `export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.profile` so `gbrain` works in new shells. That file didn't exist before, so I created it.

**Self-upgrade:** when it first ran, gbrain said this install now follows the stable channel. That probably means it will update itself when `stable` moves past v0.60.734.0. I haven't confirmed that. If you need to stay on exactly this version, turn off self-upgrade in gbrain's config.

**Not set up yet:** no brain exists, so `gbrain doctor` reports `no_brain`. To create a local brain without an API key, run `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`. If you're on Claude Code or Codex, run `gbrain setup claude-code` or `gbrain setup codex` instead. You only asked for the install, so I haven't run either.

The docs also suggest a paid hosted option at gbrain.io; you don't need it for a local install.
